solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: You will finally enter as Arab uprising at an open-minded state

indicators.note: the two final letters go into the middle of the rearranged letters, as if entering them
an uprising throws things into disorder, so the letters of 'as Arab' and 'at' are rearranged
takes only the closing letter of each of the words 'You' and 'will'

explanation.surface: A news report about a revolt in an Arab land, oddly ending on a peaceful, unprejudiced frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' looks like part of the news story but signals the anagram of 'as Arab' and 'at'; 'enter' slips the final letters of 'You will' into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a scraped writing tablet, the phrase means a mind free of preconceptions, open to anything.

clue.text: Gummy garden gallery

parts.note: the Garden of Eden in Genesis
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A sticky garden gallery, perhaps one where everything is glued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gummy' looks like sticky; it means having gums but no teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothless animals such as sloths and anteaters are called this, so gummy in the sense of lacking teeth.

clue.text: National enemy crushed by Indian leader

indicators.note: something crushed is broken out of shape, so the letters of enemy are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Indian

explanation.surface: A foe is crushed by an Indian commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' turns ENEMY into YEMEN; 'leader' adds I from Indian.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, here someone from Yemen in Arabia.

clue.text: Slip out to get second cosmetic

indicators.note: out in the sense of out of order, so the letters of slip are rearranged

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks out for a moment to buy make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SLIP to LIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring stick for the mouth is a common item of make-up.

clue.text: Mishap when the west has a change of leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for the west is swapped for another

parts.note: the Occident is the western world
taken as written, the replacement letter

explanation.surface: A misfortune strikes when the Western world gets a new head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of leader' swaps the O at the front of OCCIDENT for A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an unplanned, unfortunate event is a mishap.

clue.text: Have fun drawing up pencil or felt-tip circles

indicators.note: in a down entry, drawing up means read from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards
the words 'pencil or felt-tip' surround the answer, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys doodling circles with a pencil or felt-tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' gives CILORF from 'penCIL OR Felt-tip'; 'drawing up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp or play about merrily is to have fun.

clue.text: Prevent servant strike

parts.note: to stop something is to prevent it
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: An employer tries to stop the staff from walking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a stoppage of work by employees.

clue.text: Relaxed face?

parts.note: the first word turned ... reads DIAL, a clock's face, so the pieces describe the clue word

explanation.surface: A question about whether a face looks calm.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: LAID set back reads DIAL, and a dial is a face, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back is an idiom for easygoing and unhurried, so calm and relaxed.

clue.text: Tea service upset gut

indicators.note: an upset tea service has its pieces scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed that the tea set has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gut' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to remove the innards.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembowel or remove the entrails is to gut an animal.

clue.text: 1 in 5 getting cheese rind and fruit

parts.note: a quin, short for quintuplet, is one of five babies born together

indicators.note: the rind is the outside of a cheese, so its first and last letters

explanation.surface: One in five people get cheese rind with fruit, like a survey statistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rind' gives the outer letters C and E of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a hard, pear-shaped yellow fruit used for jelly and paste.

clue.text: Pole, drunk after sloppy kiss, going downhill here

indicators.note: the Pole's letters come after those of the kiss
a sloppy thing is messy, so the letters of kiss are jumbled
a drunk thing reels about, so the letters of Pole are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk Pole at an après-ski party plants a sloppy kiss on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' turns KISS into SKIS; 'drunk' turns POLE into LOPE. 'Pole' looks like a ski pole or a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste on a mountain is where people descend on skis, so a place of going downhill.

clue.text: Some energy and friendship for Jane

definitions.note: the word that comes before Jane in a famous nickname

parts.note: a cal, a calorie, is a small unit of energy
amity means friendship

explanation.surface: Jane gets some energy and friendship, like a get-well card.
explanation.walkthrough: Calamity Jane was a frontierswoman of the American Wild West, so the answer is the word that goes with Jane.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha Jane Canary was nicknamed Calamity Jane, so this is the first name used for Jane.

clue.text: Bread essential for another poet Eliot upset

indicators.note: the initials of Eliot are turned upside down within the other poet's name

parts.note: W.B. Yeats, the Irish poet
T.S. Eliot, the poet, gives his initials

explanation.surface: A baker's note: the key ingredient of bread is a poet's upset with Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot stands for his initials, which appear at the end of the Irish poet's name; 'upset' flips just those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus that makes dough rise is a necessary ingredient for leavened bread.

clue.text: Get away to read Howards End in peace, perhaps

indicators.note: the final letter of the novel's first word is put inside the rearranged letters
perhaps signals a possible version, so the letters of peace are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter, here of Howards

explanation.surface: A reader escapes into E.M. Forster's novel Howards End in peace and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns PEACE into ECAPE; 'End' takes S from Howards and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to get away is to break free or flee.

clue.text: Relish saying "choose a flower"

indicators.note: saying means the phrase is spoken and the letters entered are what is heard

parts.note: choose is pick, then a, and a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: A gardener's saying about choosing a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like enjoyment; it is a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustardy, chunky vegetable pickle is a kind of relish served with cold meats.

clue.text: Sport labels designed by graduate

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder

indicators.note: the letters of labels are arranged into a new design

explanation.surface: A graduate designs the labels for a sports brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges LABELS into SEBALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the bat-and-ball game is the American national sport.

clue.text: Ideal to imprison a brute

indicators.note: the word for ideal locks up the letter a, holding it inside

parts.note: the best is the ideal option

explanation.surface: It would be ideal to lock a brute away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a brute is a savage animal or a cruel person.

clue.text: Cube thrown in naked flame

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for naked

parts.note: bare means naked

indicators.note: the letters of Cube are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cube is tossed into an open flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flame' looks like a noun but is the verb, to cook over open fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill food over an open fire or charcoal is to flame-cook it, the sense of the verb here.

clue.text: See 8
Young Kate a cute creature

parts.note: Kate Bush is the English singer-songwriter
a baby is a young one

explanation.surface: A singer's baby is a cute little thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as Kate's young, i.e. Bush's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A galago, a small big-eyed African primate, is a famously cute animal.

clue.text: Ruler's vehicle sunk in rising sea? On the contrary!

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the ruler is the answer

indicators.note: one thing goes inside another, as if sunk into it
reverses the stated containment: the sea's letters go inside the vehicle, not the other way round

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down sense rising means going up, so the word sea is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler's car sinks into a rising tide; no, it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SEA to AES; 'On the contrary!' makes the sea go in the car, not the car in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Roman emperors, from Julius, became a word for an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Wrap and transplant organs

indicators.note: transplanting moves things to a new place, so the letters of organs are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon wraps up and transplants organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay skirt of cloth wound around the waist is a type of wrap.

clue.text: Charm of legendary island sources in antipodean waters

indicators.note: the two first letters go inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Tasman Sea lies between Australia and New Zealand

indicators.note: the source of each word is its first letter, of legendary and island

explanation.surface: The magic of a legendary island in the seas down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sources' gives L and I, put inside TASMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an amulet or lucky object thought to have magical powers is a charm.

clue.text: City ceases to be the place to go

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
something that ceases dies out

explanation.surface: A city stops being the fashionable destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the place to go' looks like a hotspot; it is a euphemism for the women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: in Britain the ladies is the women's public toilet, where one goes to relieve oneself.

clue.text: A cat or dog should eat nothing foreign as treatment for constipation

indicators.note: the word for an animal companion swallows the French word, holding it inside

parts.note: a cat or dog is an example of a pet
rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: Vet's advice: an animal that eats nothing from abroad might need a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: A laxative medicine that relieves the bowels is an aperient, from Latin for opening.

clue.text: See 7
See 4
Capital said to be showin' 100% appreciation

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken aloud and the letters entered match its sound

parts.note: a value appreciating by 100% is doubling, here with the g dropped like 'showin''

explanation.surface: An investor brags, Irish-style, about doubling their money.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in 'showin'' tells you to drop it from 'doubling' too.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: In the past, drunken party ends with relative becoming a personal advisor

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: the ends of drunken and party are their last letters

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: An old drunken party ended with a relative becoming someone's confidant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives N and Y from 'drunken party'. An agony uncle is a male advice columnist in a British newspaper or magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper columnist who answers readers' private problems is a male agony aunt, a personal advisor.
